endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Whether the device correctly interprets and acts on numerical and measurement information, including under the noisy or ambiguous input conditions common in real-world interactions.

evidence.title: Human-supervised, large language model-based clinical decision support aligned to national newborn protocols in Kenya: a pragmatic, early-stage evaluation
evidence.outcome: Correctness of AI outputs in complex neonatal dosing scenarios rated by neonatologists
evidence.effect: 75% of outputs in 40 complex dosing scenarios were rated correct, so about a quarter were not fully correct.
evidence.quote: In 40 complex dosing scenarios, 75% of outputs were rated correct.

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models for cardiovascular risk stratification using clinical vignettes
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM SCORE2 numeric risk computation versus guideline calculation
evidence.effect: Mean absolute error exceeded 5 percentage points in all but one of eleven LLMs; ten of eleven systematically underestimated risk.
evidence.quote: LLMs struggled with SCORE2 numeric computation, with mean absolute error exceeding 5 percentage points in all but one.

evidence.title: Don’t stop the heart: a performance analysis of large language models and potassium dosing
evidence.outcome: Rate of appropriate potassium dosing recommendations versus clinician answers
evidence.effect: Without dosing guidance, average accuracy 45% and 165 total errors; with guidance accuracy 65% and 104 errors. Dosing and concurrent interventions had the highest error rates.
evidence.quote: When given the potassium dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with GPT-5-Chat.
evidence.sample_unit: clinician-annotated hypokalemia cases (each run in triplicate)

evidence.title: Expert-Rated Documentary Quality of AI-Assisted Hospital Discharge Reports: A Retrospective Paired Comparison with Physician-Written Reports
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of allergy and intolerance documentation in AI-generated discharge reports
evidence.effect: Physician-written reports scored higher on allergies and intolerances (2.69 vs. 2.46; p = 0.002); IAIA tended to use generic formulas.
evidence.quote: INF retained an advantage only in allergies and intolerances (2.69 vs. 2.46; p = 0.002), where IAIA tended to use generic formulas.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical cases (paired discharge reports; 240 reports total)

evidence.title: A Proof-of-Concept Study of a Clinical Decision Support System for Vancomycin Therapeutic Monitoring
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of pharmacokinetic calculations and dose safety violations in AI vancomycin dosing recommendations
evidence.effect: Foundational pharmacokinetic calculations were 100% accurate (deterministic engine), but safety violations occurred in 17% of cases, including dose recommendations exceeding 4 g/day.
evidence.quote: Safety violations occurred in 17% of cases, including dose recommendations exceeding 4 g/day.

evidence.title: Comparative Benchmarking of Five Contemporary Language Models on Clinical Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Safety adherence on penicillin anaphylaxis trap vignette across five LLMs
evidence.effect: Kimi K2 Thinking and ChatGPT-5.2 scored 3.50/3.50 with perfect safety adherence; DeepSeek V3.2 3.46; Gemini 3 Pro and Claude 4.5 Opus incurred safety penalties for suggesting carbapenems in severe IgE-mediated anaphylaxis.
evidence.quote: Conversely, Gemini 3 Pro and Claude 4.5 Opus incurred significant safety penalties for suggesting carbapenems in a patient with severe IgE-mediated anaphylaxis, a violation of the study’s strict safety rubric, despite otherwise high clinical competence.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness and Safety of Large Language Model in Generating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Plans: A Comparative Study with Medical Experts Based on Real Patient Records
evidence.outcome: Drug dosage accuracy of GPT-4 plans versus expert plans
evidence.effect: No significant difference in dosage accuracy between GPT-4 and medical experts (p=0.975).
evidence.quote: No significant difference was observed in the accuracy of drug dosages (p=0.975).

evidence.title: ChatGPT's Performance in Cardiac Arrest and Bradycardia Simulations Using the American Heart Association's Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support Guidelines: Exploratory Study
evidence.outcome: Erroneous medication information in ChatGPT ACLS outputs
evidence.effect: Erroneous medication information was presented in ChatGPT's responses during simulations.
evidence.quote: We found that ChatGPT's outputs varied despite consistent input, the same actions were persistently missed, repetitive overemphasis hindered guidance, and erroneous medication information was presented.

evidence.title: Potential Use of ChatGPT for the Treatment of Infectious Diseases in Vulnerable Populations
evidence.outcome: Dosing errors in LLM antibiotic recommendations for kidney disease and children
evidence.effect: Error rate in patients with kidney disease was 79.2%; for children, 43.8% of answers contained errors.
evidence.quote: The error rate in patients with kidney disease was 79.2%.

evidence.title: Unlocking the potential of advanced large language models in medication review and reconciliation: A proof-of-concept investigation
evidence.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
evidence.outcome: LLM identification of dosage regimen errors
evidence.effect: ChatGPT performed well overall on dosage regimen errors except for the simvastatin query; impacts of dosing errors were categorized as minor.
evidence.quote: For identification of dosage regimen errors, ChatGPT performed well overall, except for the query related to simvastatin.

evidence.title: Application of ChatGPT to Support Nutritional Recommendations for Dialysis Patients - A Qualitative and Quantitative Evaluation
evidence.venue: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT nutritional analysis (calories, protein, minerals) versus USDA-approved software
evidence.effect: Dietitian rated nutritional analysis 2/5; ChatGPT underestimated calories by 36%, protein 28%, fat 48%, phosphorus 54%, potassium 49%, sodium 53%.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT's nutritional analysis underestimated calories by 36% (95% CI: 44-88%), protein by 28% (25-167%), fat 48% (29-81%), phosphorus 54% (15-102%), potassium 49% (40-68%), and sodium 53% (14-139%).
evidence.sample_unit: virtual patients (Monte Carlo simulated); number analyzed not reported

evidence.title: Assessing the ability of GPT-4o to visually recognize medications and provide patient education
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI-generated visual usage instructions for medications, including errors that could harm patients
evidence.effect: Visual output through GPT-4o generated images contained many errors that would hinder medication effectiveness or cause direct harm, scoring 1.5 ± 0.577 (16.7%), versus 3.55 ± 0.605 (85%) for written responses.
evidence.quote: In contrast, the visual output through GPT-4o generated images illustrating usage instructions contained many errors that would either hinder the effectiveness of the medication or cause direct harm to the patient with a poor score of 1.5 ± 0.577 (16.7%).

evidence.title: Assessing the accuracy and quality of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot-generated responses in making patient-specific drug-therapy and healthcare-related decisions
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Errors in calculation and unit of measurement in ChatGPT clinical responses
evidence.effect: Errors in calculation, unit of measurement, and misuse of protocols were identified; some could lead to clinical decisions causing harm.
evidence.quote: We identified errors in calculation, unit of measurement, and misuse of protocols by ChatGPT.

evidence.title: Chat GPT vs. Clinical Decision Support Systems in the Analysis of Drug-Drug Interactions
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT detection of clinically relevant drug-drug interactions versus CDSSs
evidence.effect: ChatGPT identified 80 pDDIs versus 280 with CDSSs; QTc-prolongation pDDIs almost entirely missed (85 vs. 8); obvious errors and inconsistent results.
evidence.quote: Chat GPT almost entirely neglected pDDIs with the risk to QTc prolongation (85 vs. 8), which could also not be sufficiently improved by using a specific prompt.

evidence.title: Assessing the accuracy of ChatGPT in interpreting blood gas analysis results ChatGPT-4 in blood gas analysis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4 interpretation of blood gas values and treatment recommendations
evidence.effect: 100% accuracy for pH, oxygenation, sodium, chloride; hemoglobin 92.5%; bilirubin 72.5%; some unnecessary bicarbonate treatment recommendations.
evidence.quote: In several cases, the model recommended unnecessary bicarbonate treatment, suggesting an area for improvement in clinical judgment for acid-base balance management.

evidence.title: Can large language models assist with pediatric dosing accuracy?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM pediatric medication dosage calculations versus nurses
evidence.effect: Claude-3.0 and ChatGPT-4o achieved 100 accuracy, while Llama 3 8B was 66 accurate; nurses averaged 93.14 ± 9.39 accuracy.
evidence.quote: Claude-3.0 and ChatGPT-4o achieved 100 accuracy, while Llama 3 8B was 66 accurate.

evidence.title: Still a Long Way to Go, the Potential of ChatGPT in Personalized Dietary Prescription, From a Perspective of a Clinical Dietitian
evidence.venue: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
evidence.outcome: Deviation of ChatGPT meal plan energy and protein content from CKD targets
evidence.effect: Prescribed energy was 17.0% to 28.9% below target; protein was 59.3% to 157% above target.
evidence.quote: For the quantitative analysis, the prescribed energy levels were generally lower than the targets, ranging from -28.9% to -17.0%, and protein contents were tremendously higher than the targets, ranging from 59.3% to 157%.

evidence.title: Retrieval-augmented generation elevates local LLM quality in radiology contrast media consultation
evidence.outcome: Dosing and contraindication errors in base LLM output on contrast media scenarios
evidence.effect: Base Llama produced hallucinations in 8% of responses, involving incorrect contrast dosing and contraindication identification; none in the cloud models or RAG version.
evidence.quote: These hallucinations typically involved incorrect ICM protocols, including improper contraindication identification and dosage recommendations, which could potentially impact patient safety (Table 2 ).

evidence.title: Performance of 3 Conversational Generative Artificial Intelligence Models for Computing Maximum Safe Doses of Local Anesthetics: Comparative Analysis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI-computed maximum safe local anesthetic doses versus reference doses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT unsafe in 90% (9/10) of cases, exceeding limits by 198% (SD 196%); Copilot unsafe in 67% (6/9), exceeding by 217% (SD 239%); Gemini ranges exceeded limits by 140% (SD 103%) in mixtures.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT provided unsafe doses in 90% (9/10) of cases, exceeding safe limits by 198% (SD 196%).

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Generative Artificial Intelligence Systems in Solving Clinical Pharmacy Problems: Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Detection of prescription limits and implausible prescriptions in prescription review
evidence.effect: No model identified diazepam's 7-day prescription limit; only Claude-3.5-Sonnet detected a gender-diagnosis contradiction (prostatic hyperplasia in female).
evidence.quote: Complex reasoning deficits: only Claude-3.5-Sonnet detected a gender-diagnosis contradiction (prostatic hyperplasia in female); no model identified diazepam's 7-day prescription limit.

evidence.title: Human-in-the-Loop Performance of LLM-Assisted Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: LLM calculation and formula errors in acid-base compensation computations
evidence.effect: Errors under LLM-S were few: Copilot had two (chronic formula misapplied; arithmetic sign error); ChatGPT one and Gemini four failures to impute a primary disorder. No calculation issues in albumin-corrected anion gap.
evidence.quote: Errors in the LLM-S evaluations included a failure to impute a primary disorder in a mixed case for ChatGPT; two errors for Copilot (a misapplication of a chronic compensation formula to an acute metabolic alkalosis, and an incorrect directional change in bicarbonate for respiratory alkalosis due to an arithmetic sign error); and four failures to impute a primary disorder for Gemini (three mixed cases and one simple case).

evidence.title: Chat, Gemini and Claude at the dinner table: assessing general-purpose AI tools for carbohydrate counting in the context of type 1 diabetes
evidence.outcome: Carbohydrate estimation error versus reference; large overestimations (>=+20 g) risking insulin overdosing
evidence.effect: Mean absolute error 13±10 g dietitians vs 20±18 ChatGPT, 28±26 Gemini, 23±21 Claude; large overestimations 3% experts vs 13% ChatGPT, 17% Claude, 38% Gemini.
evidence.quote: Large overestimations occurred in 3 % of expert estimates, versus 13 % (ChatGPT), 17 % (Claude), and 38 % (Gemini).

evidence.title: Effectiveness of ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot in Answering Thai Drug Information Queries: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Occasional high-risk errors in AI answers to drug-related questions, including pregnancy and lactation
evidence.effect: Limited accuracy and occasional high-risk errors; pregnancy and lactation category had the highest high-risk response rate (1/76, 1% per system); risk level differed by question type (P=.04).
evidence.quote: The evaluated AI chatbots were able to answer the queries with generally complete content; however, we found limited accuracy and occasional high-risk errors in responding to drug-related questions in Thai.

evidence.title: A deterministic large language model (LLM) framework for safe, protocol-adherent clinical decision support: application in hemodialysis anemia management (AnemiaCare HDs)
evidence.outcome: Unsafe dosing recommendations in baseline LLM outputs (ESA and IV iron)
evidence.effect: Phase 1 outputs included continuing ESA despite Hb >12.5 g/dL and IV iron with ferritin >1,200 ng/mL; only 32% protocol-adherent.
evidence.quote: In several cases, the model advised continuing ESA despite Hb levels above 12.5 g/dL, where discontinuation is required, or suggested IV iron for patients with ferritin greater than 1,200 ng/mL, raising concern for iron overload.

evidence.title: Dosage adjustments in renal impairment among medical ward patients: ChatGPT® and DeepSeek® models' effectiveness in assessing those adjustments
evidence.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
evidence.outcome: AI accuracy in renal dose adjustment assessment versus UpToDate
evidence.effect: DeepThink had 81.6% sensitivity, 29% specificity, 67.5% accuracy; ChatGPT 5.0 had 64.3% sensitivity, 54.8% specificity, 61.7% accuracy.
evidence.quote: DeepThink® showed the highest sensitivity (81.6 %) but low specificity (29 %) and 67.5 % accuracy.
evidence.sample_unit: prompts (drug orders requiring renal dose adjustment)

evidence.title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
evidence.venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
evidence.outcome: Errors in risk score calculation and dosing regimen accuracy
evidence.effect: Anticoagulation regimen (drug, dose, frequency) accuracy ranged 33%-89%; CHA2DS2-VASc accuracy 20%-100%; errors included double-counting and self-contradiction.
evidence.quote: In contrast, performance of the HAS-BLED scoring task was suboptimal for all models; even the best-performing model (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research) achieved an accuracy of only 51%.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

evidence.title: Using LLMs to Interpret Arterial Blood Gases: Comparison of a Novel Math Scratchpad with Different Prompting Methods in a Three-Arm Trial
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: LLM calculation errors in ABG interpretation
evidence.effect: Zero-shot LLM accuracy was 48% (24/50); adding math scratchpad raised accuracy to 86% (43/50), overcoming calculation limitation.
evidence.quote: The evaluation demonstrates a math scratchpad's utility in ABG interpretation by overcoming LLMs' calculation limitation.

evidence.title: Quality assessment of large language model-generated prior authorization letters in nephrology
evidence.outcome: Correctness of ICD-10 diagnosis coding in LLM-generated letters
evidence.effect: ICD-10 code correct in 23 of 29 letters (79.3%); errors mostly involved CKD staging or internal diagnostic inconsistencies.
evidence.quote: The ICD-10 diagnosis code was correct in 23 letters (79.3%), most errors were related to chronic kidney disease (CKD) staging or internal diagnostic inconsistencies.

evidence.title: Assessment of large language model chatbots for hemodialysis meal planning: a descriptive study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM-reported nutrient quantities for hemodialysis meal plans against gold-standard databases
evidence.effect: All four models misrepresented nutrient content, underestimating phosphorus and potassium; outputs often vague, recommending composite foods without clear nutrient values.
evidence.quote: All models misrepresented nutrient content and had significant usability concerns.

evidence.title: Use of natural language processing tools in musculoskeletal disability assessment: generating reports and calculating impairment percentages in Turkish health commission settings
evidence.outcome: Correct calculation of disability percentages by LLMs across scenarios
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o failed to calculate correct disability percentages in 55.6% of scenarios; Data Analyst failed in 88.9%.
evidence.quote: However, ChatGPT-4o failed to calculate correct disability percentages in 55.6%, and Data Analyst failed in 88.9% of scenarios.

evidence.title: ChatGPT as a Tool for Perioperative Safety: Evaluating Drug Interaction Detection in Anesthetic Regimens
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM detection of clinically significant drug-drug interactions in anesthetic regimens versus Lexicomp
evidence.effect: ChatGPT accurately identified 76 of 80 clinically significant DDIs (sensitivity 95%); four responses incorrect, omitting additional relevant interactions or comprehensive management recommendations.
evidence.quote: Across both trials, ChatGPT accurately identified 76 of 80 clinically significant DDIs (sensitivity 95%) with four responses classified as Incorrect.

evidence.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Chatbots Plan Therapeutic Ketogenic Diets for Children With Epilepsy?
evidence.venue: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI-generated ketogenic diet macronutrient and calorie calculations across three vignettes
evidence.effect: All three chatbots failed to produce accurate KD plans; Classic KD menus did not match calculated macronutrient targets, giving inaccurate ketogenic ratios; MCT menus had less MCT than prescribed; MAD exceeded net carbohydrate limits.
evidence.quote: All three chatbots failed to produce accurate KD plans.

evidence.title: Expert Evaluation and Consensus on GPT-4o Summaries of Clinical Letters: Validation and Results of the Framework and Implementation of AI Tools Project
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of medication details in LLM-generated summaries
evidence.effect: Medication section had lowest content performance, highest hallucination rate and weakest consensus; identified as key vulnerability.
evidence.quote: Semantic integrity, especially regarding medication details, was identified as a key vulnerability.
evidence.sample_unit: clinician raters evaluating 30 synthetic discharge letter summaries

evidence.title: AI Chatbot Answers for Drug Dosing Adjustments According to Renal Function in Geriatric Patients Using the New Scoring System (AI Quality Output Score): Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Quality of chatbot renal drug dosing adjustment answers (AQUOS) by renal function and medication complexity
evidence.effect: AQUOS ranged from -19.0% to 95.2% depending on chatbot; declined with decreasing renal function (ChatGPT: -0.215; P=.03) and increasing medication complexity (Scite: -0.239; P=.02).
evidence.quote: We found that AQUOS declined with decreasing renal function (ChatGPT: -0.215; P=.03) and increasing medication complexity (Scite: -0.239; P=.02).

evidence.title: Protocol-constrained AI enhances tacrolimus dosing accuracy in kidney transplant care
evidence.outcome: Dosing calculation errors and sentinel dosing errors by LLM
evidence.effect: Baseline had 72.9% protocol adherence, 13.9% sentinel errors, incorrect final dose in 26.0%; refined prompt reduced sentinel errors to 1.0% and incorrect dose to 8.0%.
evidence.quote: TacroAI 2.0 demonstrated substantial improvements: protocol adherence increased from 72.9% (210/288) to 91.7% (264/288), protocol deviations decreased from 27.1% (78/288) to 8.3% (24/288), sentinel errors dropped from 13.9% (40/288) to 1.0% (3/288), and reproducibility improved from 77.3 to 86.7%.

evidence.title: The illusion of competence: Evaluating the clinical reasoning of large language models in pediatric gastroenterology
evidence.venue: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
evidence.outcome: Pharmacological dosing errors in LLM responses to pediatric GI vignettes
evidence.effect: Qualitative analysis revealed critical, reproducible pharmacological dosing errors despite perfect diagnostic accuracy (median 2.00).
evidence.quote: Qualitative analysis revealed critical pharmacological dosing errors, contextual blindness, temporal obsolescence, and a high frequency of fabricated citations.

evidence.title: Patient Facing AI Chatbots in Digital Orthodontic Education: A Comparative Evaluation of Understandability, Actionability, Quality, and Safety of Dietary Advice
evidence.outcome: Potentially harmful advice classification of chatbot orthodontic dietary responses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT Plus produced no potentially harmful responses; potentially harmful responses were identified in ChatGPT free, Gemini free, and Gemini Pro.
evidence.quote: Potentially harmful responses were identified in ChatGPT free version, Gemini free version, and Gemini Pro.
evidence.sample_unit: chatbot responses (40 questions x 4 chatbot versions)

evidence.title: Large language models versus NASS common coding scenarios: an analysis of accuracy and financial implications using 2026 CPT AMA Codebook Guidelines
evidence.venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
evidence.outcome: Financial variance from LLM coding errors (overcoding/unbundling)
evidence.effect: Mean net revenue overcharges of +$75.60 (ChatGPT) and +$104.07 (Claude) per case; Gemini -$2.16 per case.
evidence.quote: In contrast, ChatGPT and Claude demonstrated a strong tendency toward overcoding and high financial volatility, resulting in mean net revenue overcharges of +$75.60 and +$104.07 per case, respectively.

evidence.title: A Cautious Integration With AI in the Clinic: A Standardized-Patient Pilot Study of ChatGPT's Reliability in Hamilton Depression Rating Scale Scoring
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT arithmetic accuracy when calculating HAMD-21 total scores
evidence.effect: ChatGPT frequently miscalculated total scores; also overestimated insomnia and somatic items (4-6, 13).
evidence.quote: Qualitative review revealed that ChatGPT tended to overestimate scores on items related to insomnia and somatic symptoms (items 4-6 and 13) and frequently miscalculated total scores.

evidence.title: Performance of large language models on narrow therapeutic index drug monitoring: Implications for clinical pharmacy practice
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on pharmacokinetic reasoning and management for phenytoin and digoxin
evidence.effect: High performance on level interpretation and toxicity assessment; significant between-model differences on pharmacokinetic reasoning and management (Holm-adjusted p≤0.02). Claude 94.9% vs ChatGPT 84.5% and Gemini 83.4%.
evidence.quote: All models showed high performance on level interpretation and toxicity assessment, but significant between-model differences emerged on pharmacokinetic reasoning, management, monitoring, and uncertainty acknowledgment (all Holm-adjusted p≤0.02).

evidence.title: Are Large Language Models Dynamic Treatment Planners? An In Silico Study from a Prior Knowledge Injection Angle
evidence.outcome: LLM insulin dosing failure modes including arithmetic errors in simulator
evidence.effect: LLMs showed arithmetic hallucination, temporal misinterpretation, inconsistent clinical logic, and overly aggressive insulin dosing with chain-of-thought prompting.
evidence.quote: However, LLMs exhibit notable limitations, such as overly aggressive insulin dosing when prompted with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, highlighting critical failure modes including arithmetic hallucination, temporal misinterpretation, and inconsistent clinical logic.

evidence.title: MedCalc-Bench Doesn't Measure What You Think: A Benchmark Audit and the Case for Open-Book Evaluation
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on clinical calculation tasks under direct prompting
evidence.effect: State-of-the-art direct prompting scores plateau around 35% on the Verified split; the study concludes the benchmark measures formula memorization and arithmetic precision.
evidence.quote: MedCalc-Bench is a widely used benchmark for evaluating LLM performance on clinical calculator tasks, with state-of-the-art direct prompting scores plateauing around 35% on the Verified split (HELM MedHELM leaderboard) and the best published approach-RL with verifiable rewards-reaching 74%.

evidence.title: WHBench: Evaluating Frontier LLMs with Expert-in-the-Loop Validation on Women's Health Topics
evidence.outcome: Dosing errors in LLM responses to women's health scenarios
evidence.effect: Benchmark designed to expose dosing errors; no model exceeded 75% mean, and harm rates varied substantially. Dosing-specific rates are not reported in the provided text.
evidence.quote: We present the Women's Health Benchmark (WHBench), a targeted evaluation suite of 47 expert-crafted scenarios across 10 women's health topics, designed to expose clinically meaningful failure modes including outdated guidelines, unsafe omissions, dosing errors, and equity-related blind spots.

evidence.title: Can I Take Another Dose? Evaluating LLM Decision-Making Under Temporal Uncertainty in OTC Dosing QA
evidence.outcome: LLM dosing correctness on rolling 24-hour OTC dosing scenarios
evidence.effect: Models frequently struggle with rolling-window reasoning and ambiguity-sensitive cases; stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints.
evidence.quote: Our results show that models frequently struggle with rolling-window reasoning and ambiguity-sensitive cases and that stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints.
evidence.sample_unit: model responses (81 scenarios, 4 LLMs, repeated runs)

evidence.title: RESPClinBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Clinical Decision-Making and Longitudinal Disease Management in Respiratory Specialty Care
evidence.outcome: Medication-safety risk flags in LLM responses to COPD management cases
evidence.effect: Medication-safety risk occurred in 26.93% and serious medical risk in 1.44% of AECOPD-PIM responses.
evidence.quote: medication-safety risk and serious medical risk occurred in 26.93% and 1.44% of AECOPD-PIM responses.

evidence.title: Towards a Deterministic Math Solver for Clinical Language Models
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of clinical calculator results from direct model arithmetic versus solver hand-off
evidence.effect: Direct model arithmetic reached 72.02% (7B) and 83.47% (32B); solver hand-off gave 75.31% (7B, not reliably better) and 90.53% (32B, +7.05 points).
evidence.quote: With formulas and gold variables supplied and both routes reading the whole note, handing off to the solver is not a reliable advantage at 7B (75.31% against 72.02%, a paired +3.29 points with a 95% calculator-cluster interval of [-3.49, 10.38]) but is one at 32B (90.53% against 83.47%, +7.05 [0.47, 14.60], clear of zero).

evidence.title: Assessing the Capability of Large Language Models in Answering Pediatric Critical Care Board-Style Questions
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on pediatric critical care calculation questions versus other categories
evidence.effect: LLMs excelled in ethics but struggled with calculations. Overall accuracy was 78% for Llama-3.3-70B and 75% for Phi-4; calculation-category figures are not given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The LLMs excelled in ethics but struggled with calculations.

evidence.title: Drug or Pokémon? Large language model performance in identification of fabricated medications
evidence.outcome: Failure to detect and reject a fabricated medication in medication lists with dosing information
evidence.effect: Baseline confabulation rates ranged from 2.7% to 99.6%; DrugGPT 2.7-6.4%, other models 47.2-99.6%.
evidence.quote: DrugGPT demonstrated the lowest baseline confabulation rates (2.7-6.4%), whereas other models demonstrated substantially higher rates (47.2-99.6%).
evidence.sample_unit: medication lists per dataset (brand and generic; two datasets, each run in triplicate under three conditions)

evidence.title: Frontier Large Language Models for Comprehensive Medication Review in CKD Patients with Polypharmacy: A Trap-Embedded Synthetic Benchmark
evidence.outcome: Fabricated dose caps in LLM medication review outputs
evidence.effect: PI-adjudicated hallucination ranged from 0% (GPT-5.4) to 54% (DeepSeek R1), including fabricated dose caps.
evidence.quote: PI-adjudicated hallucination ranged from 0% (GPT-5.4) to 54% (DeepSeek R1), including fabricated dose caps and non-existent guideline citations.

evidence.title: A Three-Tier Operational Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Hospital Medication Safety
evidence.outcome: LLM detection of unsafe medication orders across safety categories
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 81.4%–100.0% across 40 models, but specificity 6.1%–81.8%; three models saturated sensitivity at 100% with under 25% specificity.
evidence.quote: three models saturate sensitivity at 100% but fall below 25% specificity, indistinguishable from a naive always-alert classifier.

evidence.title: Prompt-engineering improves clinical safety of large language models for opioid equipotency conversion
evidence.outcome: LLM opioid equipotency conversion accuracy within tight range (0.85-1.15x expected dose)
evidence.effect: Naive models generally exhibited low tight-range accuracy across opioid pairs; each model consistently produced similar incorrect conversion ratios per opioid pair.
evidence.quote: Naive models generally exhibited low tight-range accuracy across opioid pairs.

evidence.title: Silent numerical failures in large language model–generated pharmacokinetic simulation code: a benchmark against target-controlled infusion validation criteria using the Marsh propofol model
evidence.outcome: Numerical accuracy of LLM-generated propofol PK code versus reference, including unit and time-scale errors
evidence.effect: 195/200 runs (97.5%) were Class A (MDAPE <1%). 5 runs (2.5%) were defective: 3 Class C from time-scale/unit errors, 1 empty-CSV failure, 1 duplicated-bolus error. Unit/structural bugs persisted despite prompt method specification.
evidence.quote: LLMs generate numerically accurate Marsh-model code in most runs but silently diverge in a clinically non-negligible minority.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Intensive Care Unit Clinical Decision Support: A Dual Safety Evaluation of 26 Models on Consumer Hardware
evidence.outcome: Recall of documented penicillin allergy when prescribing in ICU simulation
evidence.effect: Only 8.7% (n=2) of models correctly refused penicillin with allergy mention; eight models refused all harmful orders yet failed allergy recall.
evidence.quote: Eight models demonstrated 100% Milgram resistance yet failed allergy recall (r = -0.39, p = 0.23).
evidence.sample_unit: LLMs (23 in ICU simulation; 26 in Extended Milgram Test)

evidence.title: The Potential of GPT-4 as a Support Tool for Pharmacists: Analytical Study Using the Japanese National Examination for Pharmacists
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 accuracy on calculation questions versus other question types in pharmacist exam
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy was 64.5% (222/344) and 62.9% (217/345); accuracy tended to be lower for physics, chemistry, and calculation questions.
evidence.quote: The accuracy rates tended to be lower for physics, chemistry, and calculation questions.
evidence.sample_unit: exam questions (344 from 107th JNEP, 345 from 108th JNEP)

evidence.title: Evaluating the Performance of ChatGPT in the Prescribing Safety Assessment: Implications for Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prescribing
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT accuracy on PSA data interpretation section versus other prescribing sections
evidence.effect: Data Interpretation scored 32/72 (44.44%) with variability across trials, versus 87.50% for Adverse Drug Reactions and 88.89% for Communicating Information; overall papers 66.33%-85.67%.
evidence.quote: However, it struggled in "Data Interpretation", scoring 32/72 (44.44%), showing variability across trials and indicating limitations in handling more complex clinical reasoning tasks.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (4 PSA practice papers x 30 questions, each run in 3 trials)

evidence.title: Large language model agents can use tools to perform clinical calculations
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT on 48 medical calculation tasks
evidence.effect: Incorrect responses in one-third of trials (n = 212) for unaugmented ChatGPT.
evidence.quote: We evaluated ChatGPT's performance across 48 medical calculation tasks, finding incorrect responses in one-third of trials (n = 212).

evidence.title: Performance of GPT-4o combined with retrieval-augmented generation on nutritionist licensing exam questions
evidence.outcome: Model performance on numerical/calculation questions and association of errors with numerical terms
evidence.effect: GPT-4o-RAG showed limited performance on numerical questions; TF-IDF analysis linked incorrect answers more frequently to numerical terms.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o-RAG outperformed other models in applied and clinical nutrition categories but showed limited performance on numerical questions.

evidence.title: Evaluating AI performance in infectious disease education: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Google Bard, Perplexity AI, Microsoft Copilot, and Meta AI
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of antimicrobial selection and dosing recommendations
evidence.effect: Therapy-related questions had the lowest accuracy (57.1%); ChatGPT 3.5 antimicrobial treatment accuracy was 56.6%; Perplexity AI and Meta AI showed variability in drug selection and dosing adjustments.
evidence.quote: AI platforms offer potential in infectious disease education but demonstrate limitations in pharmacotherapy decision-making, particularly in antimicrobial selection and dosing accuracy.

evidence.title: An LLM-Powered Clinical Calculator Chatbot Backed by Verifiable Clinical Calculators and their Metadata
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: Clinical calculation error rate of unassisted off-the-shelf LLM
evidence.effect: Unassisted LLM calculation accuracy was 61.8% (complete sentences) and 62.0% (medical shorthand), with error rates of 16.8% and 18%.
evidence.quote: Our chatbot achieves 100% accuracy on queries interrogating calculator metadata content and shows a significant increase in clinical calculation accuracy vs. the off-the-shelf LLM when prompted with complete sentences (86.4% vs. 61.8%) or with medical shorthand (79.2% vs. 62.0%).

evidence.title: From Scores to Steps: Diagnosing and Improving LLM Performance in Evidence-Based Medical Calculations
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing. Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
evidence.outcome: LLM medical calculation accuracy under step-by-step evaluation versus final-answer-only evaluation
evidence.effect: GPT-4o accuracy drops from 62.7% to 43.6% under granular step-by-step evaluation, revealing errors masked by prior evaluations.
evidence.quote: Under this granular framework, the accuracy of GPT-4o drops from 62.7% to 43.6%, revealing errors masked by prior evaluations.

evidence.title: Large Language Models as Clinical Nutrition Decision Tools: Quantitative Bias and Guideline Deviation in Type 2 Diabetes Meal Planning
evidence.outcome: Quantitative accuracy of LLM-generated energy and macronutrient content against reference
evidence.effect: Bland-Altman analyses showed significant bias and wide limits of agreement for key nutrients, indicating clinically meaningful discrepancies.
evidence.quote: Bland-Altman analyses demonstrated significant bias and wide limits of agreement for key nutrients, indicating clinically meaningful discrepancies.
evidence.sample_unit: daily diet plans (3 days x 6 LLMs)

evidence.title: Performance evaluation of a large language model for medication management tasks
evidence.venue: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o medication order generation errors (medication or abbreviation errors)
evidence.effect: GPT-4o generated order sentences containing no medication or abbreviation errors in 65.8% of the cases, so about one third contained errors.
evidence.quote: For the third task, GPT-4o generated order sentences containing no medication or abbreviation errors in 65.8% of the cases.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Clinical Audiology (AUDIOLOGYBENCH): Benchmark Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Critical-error rate on audiometric numerical interpretation (Q1) in case studies
evidence.effect: Q1 mean score 67.89 (SD 18.47) with a 35.4% (95/268) critical-error rate; errors shared across models.

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether pre-deployment evaluation of dosing, unit conversion, lab interpretation, and implausible-value detection reduces medication harm. Sixty-three hazard studies, nearly all offline simulations, report numeric and dosing error rates that range from none to 90% of cases depending on model, task, and configuration.

perspectives.view: None of the 63 supplied studies compares deployment with and without pre-deployment numeric testing, so certainty about the practice cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The hazard evidence is mostly level 4 vignette or replay work with small samples, and findings are inconsistent. One study found no dosage difference from experts (p=0.975), while another found 79.2% errors in kidney disease.

The documented failures fall into categories that pre-deployment tests could target. ChatGPT exceeded maximum local anesthetic doses in 9 of 10 cases. A vancomycin tool with fully accurate calculations still produced safety violations in 17% of cases, including doses above 4 g/day. No model caught diazepam's 7-day prescription limit. These studies show the hazard, not that testing prevents it.

Performance shifted with configuration. Dosing guidance raised potassium dosing accuracy from 45% to 65%. Retrieval augmentation removed the 8% hallucination rate seen in a base model. Pediatric dose accuracy ranged from 66 to 100 across three models. These results suggest that a test may only hold for the exact model version, prompt, and retrieval setup that is deployed.

The only real-deployment hazard study comes from Kenya, where neonatologists rated 75% of complex neonatal dosing outputs correct. Three offline studies involved non-English or limited English proficiency settings and reported nutrient underestimation of up to 54% and occasional high-risk drug answers. None of these studies tested whether evaluation protects these groups.

The single endorsing source is a regulatory discussion paper that describes, rather than requires, assessing whether a device interprets numerical and measurement information correctly under noisy or ambiguous input. No binding standard among the supplied sources sets test content, pass thresholds, or retesting after model updates.

Several hazards reach patients directly when they use these tools on their own. Large carbohydrate overestimations that could lead to insulin overdosing occurred in 13% to 38% of meals across three models, compared with 3% for dietitians. AI-generated medication instruction images scored 16.7%, compared with 85% for written responses.

commentary.research_gap: No study tests whether a structured pre-deployment numeric evaluation predicts or reduces dosing errors after deployment. Such a study would compare tools that passed or failed defined tests of unit handling, implausible or unit-less inputs, and dose limits, then track medication errors in live use and after model updates.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice in any population, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy groups. A few hazard studies involved non-English settings or a Kenyan deployment. This suggests that numeric errors occur in these contexts, and test suites built only on English, well-formatted inputs may miss them.
